summary: Tenant SIEM replay: missing events during gzip boundary rehydration and request for signed delivery manifest & retention mapping
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that when they rehydrate historical SIEM exports (GZIP-compressed NDJSON batches delivered to their S3 bucket), approximately 0.7% of events are missing on replay. Missing events appear to correlate with large batches that span multiple gzip member boundaries.

Impact:
- FinEdge uses the exports for AML and transaction surveillance; missing events break their replay tests and could be material for audit evidence.
- Customer requests signed delivery manifests and per-batch HMAC proofs tied to rotating KEK so they can present chain-of-custody during the upcoming compliance review.

Environment:
- Export path: s3://finedge-exports/redwood/tenant-01234/daily/2026-03-10/
- Exporter version: siem-exporter v2.3.7 (deployed in prod-us-east cluster)
- Delivery: GZIP-compressed NDJSON, file naming: tenant-01234-20260310-<batch>.ndjson.gz

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Download compressed object tenant-01234-20260310-batch-045.ndjson.gz
2) gunzip -c tenant-01234-20260310-batch-045.ndjson.gz | jq -c . > lines.jsonl
3) Count lines and compare to tokenized event ledger FinEdge receives from live webhook delivery for the same interval
4) Rehydrate with a streaming consumer that concatenates gzip members; missing ~0.7% lines compared to webhook ledger

Observed logs / customer evidence (attached links):
- Customer-supplied manifest: s3://finedge-exports/redwood/tenant-01234/manifest-20260310.json (they included counts per object)
- Sample object flagged: tenant-01234-20260310-batch-045.ndjson.gz (hash: sha256:ab12...)
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 10:30 UTC — Support triage: confirmed customer counts mismatch; reproduction attempt on staging succeeded for large multi-member gzip where last line of a member lost when streaming consumer used naive concatenation.

Hypothesis 1: exporter occasionally writes NDJSON records across gzip member boundaries and some downstream tooling that expects single-member gzip or uses non-stream-safe concatenation drops partial newline-terminated records.

Hypothesis 2: the consumer used by the customer (custom Go reader) treats 0x0A at member boundaries inconsistently; our S3 object is correct but their streaming concat logic truncates events when gzip member ends mid-record.

Findings: objects in question contain multiple gzip members. Using 'zcat' on Linux and streaming a robust gzip concatenation library preserves lines; a naive gunzip+cat pipeline in older Go stdlib in some versions may discard trailing partial buffer content.

Logs reviewed: exporter stdout from 2026-03-10 shows periodic flush() calls every ~2MB which can create new gzip members when rotation happens; exporter config in prod is default: member_threshold_bytes=2097152.

Security/Compliance note: customer requires cryptographic delivery proof. Current exports include per-object sha256 metadata in our delivery manifest but do not include per-record HMAC or a signed resume token.

2026-03-12 12:40 UTC — FinEdge (Customer): We observed missing events only on objects >8MB. We can share their consumer library and a stripped dataset. We need signed manifests and proof of rotation for KEKs for legal purposes — audit window closes 2026-03-18.

2026-03-12 15:20 UTC — Eng (SRE - Priya Desai): Reproduced the missing-lines behavior using the customer's consumer built against Go 1.17. Upgrading to Go 1.20 or using github.com/klauspost/compress/gzip fixed the truncation. Exporter-side mitigation: reduce gzip-member frequency or emit a record delimiter boundary token before flush.

2026-03-12 17:00 UTC — Security (Marcus Lee): Customer asks for chain-of-custody controls. We can offer per-object signed manifest with an Ed25519 signature and include per-batch HMAC using current KEK; will need PR to infra to emit manifests and rotation proof.

2026-03-13 09:10 UTC — Jonah Rivera (Support): Proposed short-term workaround: instruct FinEdge to rehydrate using 'zcat' or upgrade consumer library; propose medium-term: add signed-manifest output and optional per-record HMAC. Will schedule infra change as 'Task' after customer signoff.

2026-03-13 09:45 UTC — FinEdge (Customer): Accept short-term workaround for immediate replay. Please provide timeline for signed-manifest + HMAC changes — auditor requires evidence by 2026-03-18 or we must escalate contractually.
proposed_workaround:
Short-term: Customer to rehydrate using stream-safe tools (zcat, python gzip module with concatenation support, or upgrade Go runtime/third-party gzip library). We provided a one-off rehydration script and validated counts for the flagged objects.

Medium-term: Add exporter config option 'single_member_mode' and emit additional per-object manifest record containing: object_name, sha256, object_size, event_count (NDJSON line count) and an Ed25519 signature over the manifest. Also support per-batch HMAC envelope keyed with rotating KEK and publish KEK rotation metadata to KMS audit log.
